qualifying_findings.title: Spring AI MCP Streamable HTTP transport unbounded session allocation DoS
qualifying_findings.summary: Spring AI 2.0.0's MCP Streamable HTTP server transport does not bound retained sessions and does not require client authentication by default, allowing a remote attacker to exhaust memory with repeated initialize requests.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vendor advisory and NVD CVE record
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Spring AI 2.0.0; fixed in 2.0.1 OSS and 2.0.0.1 enterprise support
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP transports are agent tool-control boundaries; unauthenticated resource exhaustion can take down AI tool servers shared by legitimate agents.

qualifying_findings.title: Spring AI Semantic Cache cross-context isolation bypass
qualifying_findings.summary: Spring AI 2.0.0 Semantic Cache used a context hash that could allow cached responses to be shared across unrelated system-prompt contexts.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vendor advisory and NVD CVE record
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Spring AI 2.0.0; fixed in 2.0.1 OSS and 2.0.0.1 enterprise support
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Semantic caches can cross tenant, prompt, or policy boundaries; cache isolation failures can leak or replay responses under the wrong AI application context.

qualifying_findings.title: Spring AI tool calling boundary bypass can dispatch unadvertised tools
qualifying_findings.summary: Spring AI's tool-calling support advertised a per-request tool list to the model but did not fully enforce that list at dispatch, allowing conditions where a tool unavailable to the current request could be invoked.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vendor advisory and NVD CVE record
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Spring AI 2.0.0, 1.1.0 through 1.1.8, and 1.0.0 through 1.0.9; fixed in 2.0.1 OSS, 2.0.0.1, 1.1.9, and 1.0.10
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Advertised tool lists are least-privilege boundaries for agent execution; dispatch fallback can turn prompt influence into unintended tool access.

qualifying_findings.title: CKAN MCP Server SSRF filter bypass via hostname aliases

qualifying_findings.title: Omnigent shared agent bundle overwrite enables runner command execution
qualifying_findings.summary: Omnigent before 0.3.0 allowed an authenticated user with edit access to overwrite a shared/template agent bundle, add a stdio MCP server, and cause future sessions using that shared agent to launch attacker-controlled commands with runner permissions.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record and older GitHub security advisory

qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Shared agent templates and MCP stdio configuration are delegated-authority boundaries; bundle overwrite can turn ordinary session edit rights into runner RCE and credential exposure.

qualifying_findings.title: Omnigent agent bundle callable path imports allow runner RCE
qualifying_findings.summary: Omnigent before 0.3.0 accepted authenticated agent bundles with a dotted Python callable path; the runner could import and invoke attacker-selected callables such as subprocess.check_output, exposing files, environment variables, credentials, workspace data, internal services, and availability.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record with linked project release
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent bundle validation is an AI supply-chain and execution-sandbox control; dynamic callable imports create a direct path from user-controlled agent packaging to runner code execution.

qualifying_findings.title: Omnigent shell parser bypass allows unauthorized repository or workspace actions
qualifying_findings.summary: Omnigent before 0.3.0 failed to recognize several shell-command forms, including combined interpreter flags, wrappers, substitutions, and a background operator, causing repository and workspace allowlist policies to abstain and permit unauthorized git, gh, or workspace-escape operations.

qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Coding-agent shell policies often rely on command parsing; parser blind spots can let prompt-injected or authenticated agents bypass repository and workspace least-privilege controls.

qualifying_findings.title: Omnigent cwd traversal lets agent tools access files outside workspace
qualifying_findings.summary: Omnigent before 0.3.0 allowed an authenticated user to upload a session-scoped agent bundle with an absolute or traversal-containing os_env.cwd, making sys_os_read, write, edit, and shell tools treat attacker-selected paths as trusted roots when OMNIGENT_RUNNER_WORKSPACE was unset.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record with linked project release
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Workspace confinement is a core coding-agent safety control; cwd trust confusion can expose runner files, environment secrets, and non-workspace data to agent tools.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record

qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Local dataset and visual-model tooling can expose host files through browser-origin mistakes, affecting AI data security and developer workstation boundaries.

qualifying_findings.summary: CT Insider reported that a Connecticut Superior Court judge found hidden white-text AI instructions in legal filings that told AI systems analyzing the documents to favor the filer and reverse a clerk's ruling; the judge treated it as prompt injection and revoked electronic filing access.
